summary: Burned 50-foot pole L-4 lookout site in Pend Oreille County, WA, built 1936; sources date the fire to 1960 or 1965. Willhite's 2019 photos show a footing and a stairway.

facts.status_note: Burned; sources date the fire to 1960 or 1965. Willhite's 2019 photos show a lookout footing and a stairway.

staffing.status: named lookouts in 1943, 1951-1952 and 1956; no later staffing in the sources

access.note: Willhite gives directions from Usk up Kings Lake Road and says most cars should be able to get up. No source found says the road is closed.

visit.trail_note: Willhite labels the site drive-up. No tower stands to climb; the site has a footing and a stairway.

events.note: Built as a 50-foot pole tower with an L-4 cab
Mrs. Earl Hupp, in a 1943 Colville Examiner item (Willhite captions spell it Hump)
Nadine Barrett listed as lookout for 1951-1952
October 18, 1956 inspection found heart rot in two legs and rot in the second and third bents
January 22, 1957 cost estimate of $687.50 for leg splice, landing replacement, roof repair and repainting
Firelookout.com dates the fiery demise to 1960
Burn footage appears in the film A Fire Called Jeremiah, released 1962 (per Willhite)
Firetower.org and the Forest Lookouts site date the fiery demise to 1965; Willhite thinks a replacement tower's burn would likely be this date
Footage reused in the film Fire On Kelly Mountain (per Willhite)
Registered December 16, 2012, nominated by Ray Kresek

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Firelookout.com dates the fiery demise to 1960; Firetower.org and the Forest Lookouts site date it to 1965. Willhite places the first burn before the 1962 film and suggests 1965 was a second, replacement tower. The story gives both dates.
The 1943 Colville Examiner item, as quoted by the Forest Lookouts site and Willhite, reads Hupp; Willhite photo captions read Hump.

notes_for_editor: The fire year is disputed (1960 vs 1965) and the story keeps both. Willhite also mentions a possible crow's nest to the south that may have lasted into the 1970s and says it needs checking; not used. Present-day description rests only on Willhite's 2019 photos and captions. Access is marked public from Willhite's road directions; no closure was checked.
